subject.title: Core hardening tracker: converge duplicated runtime invariants onto single owners

question: Which verified seams should remain in this core-hardening program, and in what priority order should maintainers authorize their separate implementation PRs?
rationale: Source inspection proves duplicated ownership remains, but choosing canonical boundaries across sessions, providers, plugins, and subagent authority is an architecture and compatibility decision that automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Prioritize highest-risk seams
options.body: Keep the tracker and authorize separate work first for CLI terminal outcomes, run staleness, session access, and other rows with demonstrated behavioral drift.

options.title: Narrow to active regressions
options.body: Retain only rows with a currently demonstrated user-visible failure and move purely structural rows out of the active program.

options.title: Pause the umbrella
options.body: Stop program-level sequencing and require independently reported bugs before any further canonical-owner refactors.

recommendation.title: Prioritize highest-risk seams
recommendation.body: Keep the tracker and authorize separate work first for CLI terminal outcomes, run staleness, session access, and other rows with demonstrated behavioral drift.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history and the protected architecture signal make this person the strongest available owner for program scope and sequencing.
